newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-STEWART GRAND PRIX ANNOUNCE FIRST SPONSORSHIP DEAL.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-STEWART GRAND PRIX ANNOUNCE FIRST SPONSORSHIP DEAL.

text.p: Three times world champion Jackie Stewart on Tuesday confirmed his new Formula One team's first major sponsorship deal.
Stewart has secured 25 million sterling ($38.89 million) five-year backing from the Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation (HSBC), confirming the deal at a news conference in London.
Stewart said the agreement was the first of four or five similar deals required to meet the budget for the team's entry into Grand Prix racing next season.
HSBC is one of the world's leading international banking and financial services organisations and the biggest of its type based in London.
Stewart said he did not expect HSBC to be the team's title sponsors and gave no details about his driver line-up.

But he said he had been in touch with Britain's Damon Hill and would be delighted if he could sign him for his team, although he said he thought the 35-year-old Briton would be considering other more attractive offers from rival teams first.

Stewart said: "It would be wonderful to have Damon Hill. He would be a dream for us for two reasons. He would bring to us the number one as world champion, he has knowledge and experience of being a driver with a top team and top cars and in my opinion is a very well balanced person. Plus, I knew his mother and father very well.
"Of course he has had other offers from other teams and money to consider and we may not be able to afford him. If we could it would be a fairytale."

He said he expected the Stewart team's car to be unveiled later this year in readiness for winter testing and said he hoped the team would become competitive as soon as possible. But he said he did not expect to be able to challenge the top teams or win races in his first season.

The chairman of HSBC Sir William Purves said he had agreed to go ahead with the deal after meeting Stewart, suggesting it was a great opportunity for HSBC to establish themselves on a world-wide basis.
